a two-step transition from a 90-nm 100-GHz CMOS voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) to a W-band WR-10 wave-guide was successfully demonstrated.

the design, simulation, and measurement of a two-step CMOS to waveguide transition at W-band.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a complete transition from CMOS to W-band waveguide with wire-bonding and demonstrated the packaging of a 90-nm VCO at 100 GHz with an average loss of 2.5 dB (including the 2-cm CPW line).
we are able to package a W-band CMOS VCO with a 49% wide-band transition with an average loss of only 2.5 dB.
the proposed transition has a wide-bandwidth, low insertion loss, low reflection loss, and is compatible with standard CMOS technology.

wire-bonding can be used to connect CMOS to waveguide at W-band frequencies with reasonable loss.
wire-bonding is a feasible solution for connecting on-chip CMOs pads to a CPW line at mm-wave frequencies.
the wire-bonding approach is a promising technique to integrate CMOS with high-frequency packaging.
